transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I've been hearing voices that aren't actually there, and it's really scaring me. I've also just been feeling so incredibly depressed and completely empty for a very long time now.
Do you hear these voices only during the times when you are feeling deeply depressed, or do you also hear them even when your mood feels relatively normal?

I still hear them even when my mood feels relatively normal. There have been periods, like for a couple of weeks at a time, where the heavy depression lifted a bit, but the voices didn't stop. They seem to happen regardless of how down I am feeling.
How long has this overall struggle with the voices been going on, and would you say you have felt deeply depressed for most of that total time?
The whole struggle has been going on for about a year and a half now. And yes, I've felt deeply depressed for most of that time, probably for about nine months of it.
During those nine months when you felt deeply depressed, did you also experience other symptoms like changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, or a total loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

During those nine months, I completely lost interest in my hobbies and felt absolutely no pleasure in anything I used to enjoy. I don't really recall having major changes in my sleep, appetite, or energy levels, but the complete loss of joy was overwhelming.
During that nine-month period, did you struggle with feelings of worthlessness, trouble concentrating, or thoughts of death or suicide?

I didn't really struggle with feeling worthless, but my concentration was terrible and I couldn't even focus on reading or watching TV. I also had frequent thoughts of death, like wishing I just wouldn't wake up, though I never had a specific plan or tried to act on those thoughts.
During those nine months, did you feel physically slowed down in your movements and speech, or did you feel unusually restless and unable to sit still?
I didn't really notice either of those physical changes during that time. I don't recall feeling physically slowed down or unusually restless.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experiences active-phase psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) spanning 1.5 years, with these symptoms persisting for weeks at a time in the absence of any prominent mood symptoms. Additionally, they experienced a major depressive episode lasting 9 months, which represents a significant portion of the total duration of the illness. This clinical picture meets the criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type, distinguishing it from Schizophrenia (due to the prominent mood episode) and Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features (due to psychosis persisting outside of depressive episodes).
